title: Modular Terraform module for Prometheus/Grafana + OTel collector + log shipper (VPC-safe)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a single, opinionated Terraform module that installs and manages the observability stack in customer VPCs for Private deployments. The module should support Helm-based installs of Prometheus (community kube-prometheus-stack), Grafana, an OpenTelemetry Collector sidecar/daemonset configuration, and a configurable log shipper (Vector or Fluent Bit). Goals: 1) VPC-safe defaults with private subnets, internal ALBs where needed, and no public internet egress required for control plane; 2) clear upgrade path for chart/chart-operator versions and built-in hooks for controlled rollouts; 3) health check resources and automated remediation via Kubernetes Job or controller pattern (e.g., restart crashed pods, reconcile misconfigured CRs); 4) lightweight state outputs to integrate with Private control plane (endpoints, cert fingerprints, grafana-admin-secret-ref); 5) security posture: support for KMS-encrypted secrets, restrict Grafana to RBAC/SSO endpoints, TLS termination options. Module should be cloud-agnostic where possible (AWS-focused initially) and include test harness for smoke and chaos tests in a dedicated QA VPC.
background: Multiple customers running Private deployments requested a maintained, supported Terraform module that standardizes observability installs across VPCs. Current operator-managed stacks diverge per account; upgrades are ad-hoc and have caused incidents (slow grafana restarts, scrape config drift). Existing infra tickets (ENG-10342, ENG-14621) implemented pieces of this but we need a unified module with upgrade semantics and health automation.
acceptance_criteria: Module installs Prometheus, Grafana, OTel Collector, and a log shipper via Helm charts with configurable values
Defaults are VPC-safe: deploy to private subnets, no public LoadBalancer by default, and egress via NAT or customer-supplied endpoints
Module exposes outputs: prometheus_endpoint, grafana_internal_url, grafana_admin_secret_ref, otel_collector_endpoint, log_shipper_status_url
Has documented upgrade procedure: chart bump workflow, canary rollout option, and rollback hooks (pre/post hooks documented)

Health checks: CRON healthcheck job that verifies pod readiness, scrape targets count, and log shipper forwarding; failing checks create a k8s Job for remediation and a PagerDuty trigger (or simulated in QA)
Supports secret encryption via KMS and option to inject existing TLS certs or use cert-manager
Automated smoke tests (Helm install -> verify endpoints -> sample metric ingested -> log shipped) run as part of CI (GitHub Actions) and pass on the QA VPC
Module has upgrade tests that simulate chart version changes and validate no-data-loss rollout in CI
out_of_scope: Building a custom observability operator. Deep dashboard design for customers. Full managed alerting rules (we will ship a baseline ruleset but customers can override).
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: using Vector as default shipper gives us structured telemetry and flexible sinks but Fluent Bit has smaller footprint. Chosen approach: default to Vector with an option to flip to Fluent Bit via variable. For OTel collector, prefer deployment as DaemonSet for lower tail latency but provide option for Sidecar where needed. We will maintain a small compatibility matrix with supported Helm chart versions and k8s versions.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: module skeleton, Helm provider + values schema, basic install and outputs. Phase 2: add healthcheck cronjob + remediation jobs, KMS secret support, test harness. Phase 3: upgrade workflows, canary helm release pattern, CI upgrade tests. Phase 4: documentation, migration guide for existing customers, and handoff to SRE/support.
progress_updates: 2026-01-20 - Maya Chen: Initial design doc posted to Confluence (link below). Chose Vector as default log shipper after perf and schema flexibility evaluation.

2026-02-02 - Carlos Rivera: Terraform skeleton created and validated in dev VPC. Helm provider pinned to v2.7.1 in the module to avoid breaking changes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345
2026-02-18 - Maya Chen: Removed public LoadBalancer option by default; added optional internal ALB resource for Grafana when customers request cross-AZ access. Need infra review for ALB IAM role.
2026-02-25 - Security Review: Tanya Park: KMS integration pattern approved pending secrets handling doc. Marked security_review_required=true for follow-up.

2026-03-05 - Carlos Rivera: Implemented basic healthcheck Job and remediation Job. Observed two failure modes in QA: scrape config drift and Vector crashloop due to memory limits; added recommended resource requests/limits in values.yaml.

2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: CI smoke tests added to GitHub Actions. Test harness still flaky in noisy QA cluster; next steps: isolate QA VPC and reduce background load. CI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2419
migration_notes: Provide a migration plan for existing Private installs: 1) export current values (Helm) and secrets; 2) map to new module variables; 3) perform canary upgrade in a single namespace; 4) monitor scrape counts and retention; 5) rollback if metrics drop. Documented in Confluence.
test_plan_summary: CI will run: helm install -> basic probe (HTTP /metrics for prometheus, /api/health for grafana) -> push synthetic metric via otel collector -> assert metric visible in Prometheus -> emit test log and assert delivery in destination (S3/CloudWatch or file sink). Upgrade tests: run helm upgrade to next chart patch/minor and validate probes still pass.
pull_request_template: When opening PR for this module: include CHANGES.md with chart version bumps, list of new module variables, upgrade guidance, and results of CI smoke/upgrade tests.
